grades.quote: One source of interleaving is multiprocessor hardware: computers with multiple CPUs executing independently, such as xv6’s RISC-V. These multiple CPUs share physical RAM, and xv6 exploits the sharing to maintain kernel data structures that all CPUs read and write. This sharing raises the possibility of one CPU reading a data structure while another CPU is mid-way through updating it
grades.reason: Explains that multiple CPUs run independently and share RAM, so one CPU can read or update data while another is mid-update. It lists interrupts as a separate source of interleaving. This implies that masking interrupts on one CPU can't stop other CPUs, but it never says so explicitly.
